theory.intro: The symbol $\sqrt{\;}$ means the **non-negative principal square root**, which is positive when the number under the root is positive, so $\sqrt{25}=5$ and never $-5$. No real number squares to a negative, so $\sqrt{x}$ is **not real** when $x<0$, and $\sqrt{0}=0$.
facts: For $x>0$, $\sqrt{x}$ is the **positive** square root of $x$: $\sqrt{36}=6$, never $-6$.
$\sqrt{x}$ is **not real** for $x<0$, because no real number multiplied by itself gives a negative, and a calculator returns an error for $\sqrt{-9}$.
A minus sign **in front** of the root is fine — $-\sqrt{16}=-4$ is real — but $\sqrt{-16}$ is not.
An **even** index needs a number that is not negative underneath, but an **odd** index does not: $\sqrt[4]{-16}$ is not real, while $\sqrt[3]{-64}=-4$ is.
The equation $x^{2}=49$ has two solutions, $x=7$ and $x=-7$, but the single value $\sqrt{49}$ is $7$.
steps: Look at the index of the root: is it even or odd?
Work out the sign of the number under the root.
For an even index, a negative number gives no real root, zero gives zero, and a positive number gives the positive principal root. For an odd index, take the single real root.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}18\times18&=324\\\sqrt{324}&=18\end{aligned}$
The square-root symbol gives the positive principal root when the number under it is positive.

$\sqrt{0}=0$, since $0\times0=0$.

workedExamples.question_text: Which of $-\sqrt{196}$, $\sqrt{-196}$ and $-\sqrt{-196}$ are real? Evaluate any real expression.
workedExamples.solution_text:
In $-\sqrt{196}$, the minus sign is outside the root. Take the positive square root first, then apply the minus sign.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-\sqrt{196}\\&=-(14)\\&=-14\end{aligned}$

Both $\sqrt{-196}$ and $-\sqrt{-196}$ have a negative number under the square root, so neither is real. An outside minus sign does not change this.

workedExamples.question_text:
Determine whether each expression is real. Evaluate it if possible.
(a) $\sqrt{-(-64)}$
(b) $\sqrt{15-15}$
(c) $\sqrt{4-13}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Work out the number under the root first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{-(-64)}\\&=\sqrt{64}\\&=8\end{aligned}$
The expression is real.

(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{15-15}\\&=\sqrt{0}\\&=0\end{aligned}$
Zero is not negative, so the expression is real.

(c) $4-13=-9$. No real number squared gives $-9$, so $\sqrt{4-13}$ is not real.

workedExamples.question_text:
Determine whether each root is real. Evaluate it if possible.
(a) $\sqrt[3]{-216}$
(b) $\sqrt[5]{-1024}$
(c) $\sqrt[4]{-256}$
(d) $\sqrt[4]{2401}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The index is odd, so a negative number under the root is allowed.
$\begin{aligned}(-6)^3&=-216\\\sqrt[3]{-216}&=-6\end{aligned}$

(b) The index is odd.
$\begin{aligned}(-4)^5&=-1024\\\sqrt[5]{-1024}&=-4\end{aligned}$

(c) The index is even. Every real number raised to the fourth power is non-negative, so $\sqrt[4]{-256}$ is not real.

(d) The number under this even root is positive; take the positive principal root.
$\begin{aligned}7^4&=2401\\\sqrt[4]{2401}&=7\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Classify each expression as a surd, rational, or not real.
(a) $\sqrt{19}$
(b) $-\sqrt{\frac{81}{400}}$
(c) $\sqrt{-\frac{4}{121}}$
(d) $\sqrt[3]{-\frac{343}{512}}$
(e) $\sqrt[4]{-\frac{16}{625}}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $19$ is positive and is not a perfect square. Its square root is irrational, so $\sqrt{19}$ is a surd.

(b) The number under the root is positive; the minus sign is outside.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-\sqrt{\frac{81}{400}}\\&=-\frac{9}{20}\end{aligned}$
This is rational.

(c) The number under the square root is negative, so $\sqrt{-\frac{4}{121}}$ is not real.

(d) The index is odd, so the negative number under the root is allowed.
$\begin{aligned}\left(-\frac{7}{8}\right)^3&=-\frac{343}{512}\\\sqrt[3]{-\frac{343}{512}}&=-\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}$
This is rational.

(e) The index is even and the number under the root is negative, so $\sqrt[4]{-\frac{16}{625}}$ is not real.

workedExamples.question_text: Explain why $\sqrt{-\frac{36}{121}}$ cannot be evaluated as a real number.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Squaring a positive or negative real number gives a positive result; squaring zero gives zero. For example,
$\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{6}{11}\right)^2&=\frac{36}{121}\\\left(-\frac{6}{11}\right)^2&=\frac{36}{121}\end{aligned}$
No real number squared gives $-\frac{36}{121}$, so $\sqrt{-\frac{36}{121}}$ is not real.

foundation.question_text:
Is $\sqrt[3]{-64}$ defined?
If so, evaluate it.
foundation.solution_text:
The index $3$ is odd, so a negative number under the root is allowed.
$(-4)\times(-4)\times(-4)=-64$
$\sqrt[3]{-64}=-4$

The index $4$ is even, and a real number raised to an even power is never negative: $2^{4}=16$ and $(-2)^{4}=16$.
No real number to the fourth power gives $-16$, so $\sqrt[4]{-16}$ is not real.

foundation.question_text:
Which of $\sqrt{-49}$ and $-\sqrt{49}$ is defined?
Give its value.
foundation.solution_text:
In $\sqrt{-49}$ the negative sits under the root, so it is not real.
In $-\sqrt{49}$ the minus sign sits outside the root, so take the root first.
$-\sqrt{49}=-7$

Work out the number under the root first.
$7-10=-3$
The number under the root is negative, so $\sqrt{7-10}$ is not real.

development.question_text:
Is $\sqrt{-(-25)}$ defined?
If so, evaluate it.
development.solution_text:
Work out the number under the root first.
$-(-25)=25$
That is positive, so the root is real.
$\sqrt{-(-25)}=5$

Take the root first: $\sqrt{-1}$ needs a real number whose square is $-1$, and there is none.
Putting a minus sign in front of something that is not real does not make it real.
So $-\sqrt{-1}$ is not real.

development.question_text: Classify $\sqrt{-(-169)}$ as a surd, rational, or not real.
development.solution_text:
Work out the number under the root first.
$-(-169)=169$
$\sqrt{169}=13$, so the number is rational.

development.question_text:
Is $\sqrt[5]{-32}$ defined?
If so, evaluate it.
development.solution_text:
The index $5$ is odd, so a negative number under the root is allowed.
$(-2)^{5}=-32$
$\sqrt[5]{-32}=-2$

The index $4$ is even and $625$ is positive, so the root is real and taken as the positive value.
$5^{4}=625$
$\sqrt[4]{625}=5$

development.question_text:
Is $\sqrt{12-12}$ defined?
If so, evaluate it.
development.solution_text:
Work out the number under the root first.
$12-12=0$
The root is undefined only for negative numbers, and $0$ is not negative.
$\sqrt{12-12}=0$

development.question_text: Classify $\sqrt{-\frac{9}{16}}$ as a surd, rational, or not real.
development.solution_text:
The number under the square root is negative.
No real number squared gives $-\frac{9}{16}$, so $\sqrt{-\frac{9}{16}}$ is not real.

development.question_text: Classify $-\sqrt{\frac{49}{100}}$ as a surd, rational, or not real.
development.solution_text:
The number under the root is positive, so the root is real.
$\sqrt{\frac{49}{100}}=\frac{7}{10}$
The minus sign sits outside the root, giving $-\frac{7}{10}$, which is rational.

mastery.question_text: Classify $\sqrt[4]{-\frac{81}{256}}$ as a surd, rational, or not real.
mastery.solution_text:
The index $4$ is even and the number under the root is negative.
A real number raised to an even power is never negative, so $\sqrt[4]{-\frac{81}{256}}$ is not real.

mastery.question_text: Classify $\sqrt[3]{-\frac{125}{216}}$ as a surd, rational, or not real.
mastery.solution_text:
The index $3$ is odd, so the negative number under the root is allowed.
$\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)^{3}=-\frac{125}{216}$
$\sqrt[3]{-\frac{125}{216}}=-\frac{5}{6}$, which is rational.

mastery.question_text: Explain why $\sqrt{-\frac{25}{49}}$ cannot be evaluated as a real number.
mastery.solution_text:
Squaring a real number always gives zero or a positive result.
No real number squared gives $-\frac{25}{49}$, so $\sqrt{-\frac{25}{49}}$ is not real.
